purpose: Cross-check a named Quezon river system across historical administrative text, mangrove/salinity field studies, a conference gleaning abstract, and bounded GBIF discovery without inferring current fish presence or geometry.

sourceReviews.title: ICFAS 6 / AFSSRN F1 Book of Abstracts, 2021
sourceReviews.finding: The Kabibihan study abstract describes 102 gleaners in eleven barangays across Guinayangan (six) and Tagkawayan (five), reports 15 Mollusca macro-invertebrate species under Bivalvia and Gastropoda, and names seven orders and nine families. It does not list the 15 species by name and does not report finfish taxa.
sourceReviews.decision: River-system and mollusc-gleaning context only. No finfish assertion or named mollusc record admitted; obtain the underlying report and review rights.

sourceReviews.title: SLSU Research Program 2019, project 49
sourceReviews.finding: The official institutional listing records the Kabibihan gleaning project as completed from 2018 to 2019 and presented at the 3rd International Academic Summit in Lingayen, Pangasinan, on 27-29 November 2019.
sourceReviews.decision: Project-status and bibliographic provenance only. It does not provide taxa, methods, sampling stations, coordinates, current fish occurrence, or data reuse permission.

sourceReviews.title: SLSU Research Program 2021, entry 23
sourceReviews.finding: The SLSU listing corroborates the study title and lists authors Jofren R. Moreno, Reynalyn C. Bacay, and Edmar A. Driz.
sourceReviews.decision: Title/authorship cross-check only. It provides no underlying report, study methods, sampling stations, taxa, or reuse permission.

sourceReviews.title: Executive Order No. 78, s. 1947
sourceReviews.finding: The issuance text says Kabibihan River shall be the boundary line between Tagkawayan and Guinayangan after the transfer of Aloneros to Guinayangan, effective 1 January 1948. Senate LRB direct page access returned 403; its indexed text was cross-checked with the reproduced Lawphil issuance.
sourceReviews.decision: Historical administrative name relationship only. It supplies no coordinates, current surveyed line, waterbody geometry, or municipal-water boundary.

sourceReviews.title: JICA Final Report, July 1999: Mapping and Land Cover Assessment of Mangrove Areas in the Republic of the Philippines
sourceReviews.finding: The report describes water sampling and mangrove observations on Kabibihan River at 19 points along an approximately 15 km upstream route from the lower end of aerial-photo coverage; lower reaches are described as more saline, with changes upstream. Figure 2-1-35 was not digitized.
sourceReviews.decision: Historical tidal/salinity habitat context only. No current whole-river salinity classification, fish data, or line geometry admitted.

sourceReviews.title: Toyoda, Balagas and Minematsu, 2003, Japanese Journal of Forest Environment 45(2):65-74
sourceReviews.finding: The journal abstract identifies Kabibihan River in Quezon as one of three tidal rivers in a mangrove distribution and salinity study.
sourceReviews.decision: Independent historical habitat context only; not fish evidence or current water conditions.

sourceReviews.title: GBIF occurrence API selected CoL XR Actinopterygii search
sourceReviews.finding: Two queries for the value Kabibihan River in waterBody and locality, country PH, selected checklist/taxon filter, each returned HTTP 200 and zero indexed matches.
sourceReviews.decision: Bounded indexed-text search only. Zero is not fish absence.

taxonomy.label: Catalogue of Life Extended Release Actinopterygii

limitations: The conference abstract does not identify species names from its aggregate count of mollusc species and is not a finfish survey.
The 1947 administrative statement is historical and lacks a geometry description; it is not used as a legal or channel boundary.
The 1999 JICA measurements and 2003 mangrove paper are historical context; no current water salinity or present fish distribution is inferred.
The JICA route figure is not georeferenced in this review, and the approximate route is not adopted as a centerline.
The two GBIF zero results are bounded and do not establish fish absence.
Reuse licensing was not identified for the conference abstract, JICA PDF, or J-STAGE article; no tables, figures, coordinates, or species names were reused.
nextAction: Request or locate the full 2018-2019 SLSU project report through a publicly documented institutional route, then assess identifiers and reuse terms before extracting any records. Obtain a current official hydrographic route source before considering geometry; keep salinity variable/unknown in the app until it is supported at reach and date level.
